title: Milky Way
summary: Sharp stars and a bright core on a dark night.

blocks.note: APS-C at 18 mm: about 17 s before stars streak.

steps: Pick a moonless night, away from towns. Switch the app to **Night** theme.
Set up the tripod and point at the core (south-ish in the northern hemisphere, spring to autumn).
Manual focus: zoom the live view on a bright star and turn the ring until it's the smallest point.
Set aperture wide open, ISO 3200 and the shutter from the 500 rule.
Use the 2 s timer. Take a test shot and check the stars are points, not lines.
Too dark? Raise ISO. Too noisy? Take several frames to stack later.

items: Tape the focus ring once it's set.
Turn off long-exposure noise reduction to save time, or leave it on for cleaner single frames.
Let your eyes adapt for 20 minutes and only use red light.

steps: **Mode dial to M**. Aperture wide open, **ISO 3200** (the R10 goes to 32000).
Switch to **MF**. Magnify the live view on a bright star and turn the focus ring until it's the smallest point. **AF5 › Focus guide** can help on nearer subjects.
Shutter from the star calculator: at 18 mm on the R10's APS-C sensor, about 17 s.
Lens IS off on the tripod. The R10 has no in-body stabiliser, so the lens switch is the one that matters.
**Shooting 5 › Long exp. noise reduction:** Auto for single frames, Disable if you'll stack several.
Shoot RAW (**Shooting 1 › Image quality**). Check stars are points, not lines.
Happy with it? Save everything: **Set-up 5 › Custom shooting mode (C1, C2) › Register settings › C1**. Next time, just turn the dial to C1.
canon-r10.note: Need more than 30 s? Use Mode dial B with Shooting 7 › Bulb timer.
